summary:
We developed SpaceExploit, an interactive real-time astronaut bio-telemetry and mission hazard monitoring dashboard built with Python, Streamlit, and Plotly. Designed to address the challenge of autonomous crew health monitoring during deep-space missions, the software continuously tracks critical physiological vitals—including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), and core body temperature—alongside ambient suit radiation levels.

Using automated threshold-based anomaly detection, the system immediately flags physiological overheating, cardiovascular strain, and Solar Particle Events (SPE), providing actionable shelter or EVA-pause protocols without waiting for delayed Earth-to-space communications. Additionally, the platform integrates SHA-256 cryptographic hashing to verify telemetry payload integrity between suit sensors and habitat consoles. By combining predictive health alerts, intuitive telemetry visualization, and secure data verification, SpaceExploit helps protect astronaut safety and mission continuity in high-risk extraterrestrial environments.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

SpaceExploit is an autonomous astronaut bio-telemetry and mission hazard support dashboard built to monitor crew health and suit microclimate safety in real time. Using a dynamic physiological telemetry engine, the platform continuously tracks four critical parameters across multiple crew members: Heart Rate (60–120 bpm), Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO2: 94%–100%), Core Body Temperature (36.2°C–38.5°C), and Ambient Radiation Exposure (0.10–0.75 mSv/h). An automated rule-based anomaly engine evaluates every sensor reading against safety thresholds, instantly classifying mission status into Nominal, Warning (physiological overheating and cardiovascular strain when Heart Rate > 105 bpm and Core Temperature > 37.8°C), or Critical (Solar Particle Event alert when radiation exceeds 0.50 mSv/h).

Benefits & Intended Impact:

During deep-space, lunar, or Martian Extravehicular Activities (EVAs), communication latency between spacecraft and Earth mission control can delay emergency medical guidance by several minutes. SpaceExploit enables immediate, onboard decision-making by delivering clear, actionable safety protocols—such as pausing an EVA or seeking radiation shelter—directly to crew consoles without relying on ground-station round trips.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Programming Language: Python 3.10+

- Web Framework & UI: Streamlit

- Data Visualization & Processing: Plotly, Pandas, NumPy

- Security & Data Integrity: Python hashlib (SHA-256 cryptographic payload hashing)

- Version Control & Hosting: GitHub

Creativity & Design Considerations:

Rather than displaying raw numerical tables that cause cognitive overload during high-stress mission phases, SpaceExploit combines color-coded visual telemetry trends with instant triage banners. A key engineering factor we considered was telemetry integrity: every simulated sensor packet generates a real-time SHA-256 cryptographic hash to demonstrate tamper-proof verification between suit sensors and habitat consoles. Super Intelligence (SI) tools were utilized to assist with initial Python code scaffolding, documentation drafting, and slide deck visual generation, with all threshold logic and system architecture reviewed and integrated by the team.
